images.title: All equal points lie on AB
images.purpose: Show that a new point C equally far from X and Y lies on the same perpendicular bisector AB as A and B.
images.composition: The segment XY horizontal in the middle and the perpendicular bisector vertical through its midpoint; point C high on the line with its two equal distances, lots of white space on both sides.
exact_structure: A horizontal dark segment XY in the middle of the frame, dots and labels X (left) and Y (right).
A long vertical reddish purple (#CC79A7) line through the midpoint O of XY, labelled O, with a small square right angle mark at O.
Four dark dots on the reddish purple line: A a little above XY, C further above A, B a little below XY, D further below B, each labelled.
Two thin dashed teal (#0072B2) segments from C to X and from C to Y, each with one tick mark.
Two short grey (#6B7280) arcs, one centred at X and one centred at Y, of the same radius, crossing exactly at C.
One short caption line at the bottom of the frame.
rejection: C or D drawn off the reddish purple line
the dashed segments CX and CY drawn with visibly different lengths or different tick counts
any point on the reddish purple line other than A, B, C, D and the midpoint O
images.takeaway: Any point the same distance from X and Y lies on the one perpendicular bisector of XY.
images.description: Segment XY with its vertical perpendicular bisector carrying points A, C above and B, D below, and equal dashed lines from C to X and Y.
images.context: Shown beside the concept text and video for this concept.
images.teaching_notes: Point to C, check CX = CY from the ticks, then see that C is on the same line as A and B.

image_decisions.why: Students need to see C and D landing on the same line AB, not on a new line.
